{{Infobox academic|name=Akram Aldroubi|occupation=Mathematician, professor|education=[[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|École Polytechnique Fédérale]],<br/>[[Diplôme universitaire|DU]], 1982<br/>[[Carnegie Mellon University]],<br/>M.S., 1984; Ph.D., 1987|workplaces=[[Vanderbilt University]]<br /> (1997–present)|doctoral_students=[[Fumiko Futamura]]}}
'''Akram Aldroubi''' is an American mathematician known for his work in [[Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem|sampling theory]], [[harmonic analysis]], and their applications to [[Digital signal processing|signal]] and [[Digital image processing|image processing]] as well as biomedical data analysis.

== Education ==
Aldroubi received a [[Diplôme universitaire|diplôme]] in electrical engineering from [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]], in Switzerland, in 1982.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://math.vanderbilt.edu/aldroua/curriculmvitae.html|title=Akram Aldroubi, Professor, Dept. of Mathematics, Vanderbilt University|last=Aldroubi|first=Akram|date=2017|website=Vanderbilt University|language=en|access-date=November 19, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=126563|title=Akram Aldroubi|website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project|access-date=November 19, 2017}}</ref> He studied mathematics at [[Carnegie Mellon University]], earning his master's in 1984 and his doctorate in 1987.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Unser|first1=M.|last2=Aldroubi|first2=A.|last3=Laine|first3=A.|date=March 2003|title=Wavelets in Medical Imaging: Authors|journal=IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging|volume=22|issue=3|pages=285–288|doi=10.1109/TMI.2003.809638|issn=0278-0062}}</ref>

== Career ==
After Carnegie, Aldroubi worked as a researcher at the [[National Institutes of Health]].<ref name=":1" /> He moved to the Department of Mathematics at Vanderbilt University in 1997 where he currently holds a position of professor.<ref name=":0" /> He has worked on [[Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem|sampling theory]], [[wavelet]]s, [[Frame (linear algebra)|frame theory]] and their applications to [[Digital signal processing|signal]] and [[Digital image processing|image processing]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2002/01/17/a-new-wave|title=A new wave|date=January 17, 2002|newspaper=The Economist|access-date=November 19, 2017}}</ref>

In 2009, he was awarded the [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Foreign Scholarship]] to continue teaching and conduct research.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=July 2009|title=Fulbright Awards Announced|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200906/200906-full-issue.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=56|issue=6|page=741}}</ref> In 2014, Aldroubi was inducted as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] for "contributions to modern [[harmonic analysis]] and its applications, and for building bridges between mathematics and other areas of science and engineering."<ref>{{Cite journal|date=April 2014|editor-last=Krantz|editor-first=Steven G.|title=2014 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201404/201404-full-issue.pdf#page=88|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=61|issue=4|page=420}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|date=2017|website=American Mathematical Society|language=en-US|access-date=November 19, 2017}}</ref>
